l_papers.speaker: LUCIEN
lines: Now — business, forgive me. Papers. Jean Caillet is a fine coat but it is Sylvie's stitching; the city needs its own. For the file behind the file I need the true name — spelling exact. London confirms it, the line pays out, everything breathes easier.

A small ugly necessity, my friend: papers. The Caillet coat was country cut; Paris tailors deeper. For the real file — the one London checks — I need the true name, letter by letter. It is how the line gets paid for you, you see.

choices.text: Sylvie said my name stays behind my teeth. Ask London for it.
They call me Tex. That's all any file needs.
Boyd. Travis Boyd. Spell it how it sounds.

l_name_deflect.speaker: LUCIEN
lines: Ha! Wonderful. Exactly right — and if you had answered, I would have worried for you. London it is; slower, but slow money spends the same. You have been well taught, my careful friend.
Perfect answer! Truly — I test, you pass, everyone is prettier for it. London will send the name by the long road. Bravo. Whoever trained you, I owe them a drink.

l_name_partial.speaker: LUCIEN
lines: Tex! Of course you are. Half of Texas is flying over us and the other half is walking through my kitchen. Fine — 'Tex' goes in my little book, and London can dress it properly.
'Tex.' The great American surname. You know I have three Texes this season? Fine, fine — the book takes what it is given.

l_name_reveal.speaker: LUCIEN
lines: Boyd. B-O-Y-D, Travis. There — was that so dangerous? Now the file is real, the money is real, and you, my friend, are one signature closer to Spain.
Travis Boyd. Good. A name a man can be paid for— that the LINE can be paid for, I mean. My English, forgive it. One step closer to the mountains, monsieur Boyd.
